filter.inkscape:menu-tooltip: Like Duochrome but with three colors

tspan.tspan: COCKPIT ATTITUDE AND HEADING INDICATOR
The ATTITUDE and HEADING indicator acts as a combination artificial
horizon and compass. The indicator must undergo a periodic ALIGNMENT
procedure on the ground using the IMU angular rate sensors and
accelerometer array.
ALIGNMENT is performed automatically when the spacecraft lands on
the surface.
The black hemisphere of the ball is a visual representation of lunar
surface (ground) while the white hemisphere is sky.
The V-wing shape in front of the indicator represents the forward direction of the spacecraft.
When white/black hemisphere boundary rolls DOWN, then the spacecraft is pitching UP. When the
boundary rolls UP, then the spacecraft is pitching DOWN. When the ball rolls counter-clockwise,
the spacecraft is rolling to starboard (clockwise), and vice versa.
Along the white/black boundary, the numbers printed on the ball represent TRUE (aligned with
lunar pole) compass headings in tens of degrees, with vertical lines spaced 10 degrees apart.
Horizontal lines represent pitch angles, with lines spaced 10 degrees apart. Pitch angles of 30
and 60 degrees are marked with 3 and 6 respectively.
Once aligned, the indicator will continue to show rotation of the spacecraft relative to the
surface position and time when alignment was performed. While the spacecraft is in flight,
alignment will drift with lunar rotation, or with movement across the lunar surface.
